content:
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I am a First Class Honours Computing graduate with hands-on experience building accessible web applications using React and TypeScript, alongside Node.js and PostgreSQL experience from my final-year project. I am drawn to Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare simpler and more human.

During my software development internship at Harbourline Media, I worked on its React news site, resolving accessibility audit issues across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documented it in Storybook, and wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library. In my Tidewatch project, I developed a React and TypeScript interface and a Node.js/Express API backed by PostgreSQL. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver, and it achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.

I would bring a practical, user-focused approach to building patient-facing features, with a strong interest in accessibility and responsible handling of user data. My experience with automated unit testing, Storybook and Git-based development provides a useful foundation for contributing to a collaborative engineering team, and I am keen to deepen my experience with production backend services and the privacy requirements of health data.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and approach could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It opens with a clear qualification summary, gives relevant evidence from the Harbourline Media internship and Tidewatch project, and connects accessibility to Verdane Care’s patient-focused work. The examples are specific and credible, especially the 20+ components, Storybook documentation, testing tools, and Lighthouse score of 100. The main content limitation is that it does not make full use of several relevant, truthful qualifications already present in the candidate material, including Next.js, Git/GitHub, the wellness booking project, and native English. It also does not clearly position the candidate as an early-career applicant whose professional experience does not yet reach the stated 2+ years.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses a simple, parsing-friendly format with standard paragraphs and strong keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good for a junior React-oriented profile, but weaker for this specific full-stack posting because the letter does not mention Next.js, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or the absence of end-to-end testing experience. It also does not include exact terms such as unit testing in a prominent skills-style phrase, although the testing evidence is clear in context. There are no formatting problems or unsupported keyword stuffing issues.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with Verdane Care’s patients-first and accessibility focus. The Harbourline internship demonstrates React, accessibility remediation, reusable components, Storybook, and unit testing, while Tidewatch demonstrates Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL experience. The wellness booking site is also relevant to Verdane Care’s healthcare and appointment-booking context, but it is not mentioned. The candidate has a gap against the requirement for 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript experience. The candidate material also does not demonstrate end-to-end testing, OWASP/web-security awareness, Docker, AWS or equivalent cloud platforms, analytics/A/B testing, German, or Croatian; these are gaps rather than document defects. The letter appropriately avoids claiming healthcare experience or health-data compliance expertise.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, retain the Harbourline evidence but add the supported Git-based workflow keyword without overstating experience. For example, change the final sentence to: "I wrote unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library and contributed through Git-based development workflows." Only use this wording if the candidate’s Git/GitHub use accurately included collaborative version control; otherwise state simply that Git/GitHub is part of the technical toolkit.

MINOR: In the third paragraph, add the omitted Next.js and wellness experience to strengthen alignment with the role’s nice-to-have requirements. For example, revise the paragraph to include: "My freelance work also includes building a Next.js booking website for a yoga studio, giving me experience with a wellness-related booking context and server-side-rendering tooling." Keep the existing statement that production backend experience is an area the candidate is keen to develop, since the candidate material does not establish professional production backend experience.

MINOR: In the opening paragraph, make the experience level precise rather than allowing the statement to imply that the candidate meets the 2+ years of professional experience requirement. For example, change "with hands-on experience building accessible web applications" to "with hands-on experience from a software development internship, freelance work, and substantial academic projects." This preserves the strengths without overstating the duration of professional experience.

MINOR: If the letter is intended to be screened independently from the CV, add a short sentence near the opening stating "I am a native English speaker." This is supported by the candidate information and makes the language requirement explicit. Do not add German or Croatian because the candidate material does not support those languages.

Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, and well targeted to Verdane Care’s patient-facing, accessibility-focused work. It uses strong evidence from the internship and Tidewatch project, including measurable scope (20+ components) and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The main weaknesses are some repetition, one potentially inaccurate description of the Next.js project, and a few sentences that dilute the impact of the strongest evidence. The standalone sentence about being a native English speaker is unnecessary because English proficiency can be integrated more naturally.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard headings-free letter formatting, conventional paragraph structure, and relevant keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, accessibility, and WCAG. It does not claim unsupported end-to-end testing, NestJS, Docker, AWS, or OWASP knowledge, which is appropriate. AI screening probability is moderate to high when assessed alongside the CV because the core technology and accessibility terms are present. Keyword coverage could be improved slightly by using the job ad’s exact terms where supported, especially “automated unit testing,” “Git-based workflows,” “patient-facing features,” “web accessibility,” and “PostgreSQL.”
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s accessibility, React/TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, testing, wellness, and user-focused requirements. The strongest alignment is the internship work on accessible React components and the Tidewatch full-stack project. The letter appropriately presents healthcare privacy as an area the candidate is keen to deepen rather than claiming existing health-data experience. However, the candidate’s material does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, web-security fundamentals or OWASP Top 10 awareness, and the letter cannot overcome those experience gaps. It also does not show German or Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A/B testing experience. The letter should avoid implying production backend or healthcare experience that is not documented.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUE — In the third paragraph, replace “giving me experience with a wellness-related booking context and server-side-rendering tooling” with “giving me experience with a wellness-related booking context, Next.js, and static generation.” The candidate information supports Next.js and static generation, but does not establish server-side rendering specifically.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the first paragraph, remove the standalone sentence “I am a native English speaker.” Integrate the supported language evidence more naturally, if it is useful, by changing the opening to: “I am a First Class Honours Computing graduate and fluent English speaker with hands-on experience...” This keeps the qualification relevant without interrupting the motivation for the role.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the second paragraph, remove the repeated sentence fragment “Git/GitHub is also part of my technical toolkit.” The same point is repeated in the third paragraph. Replace the end of the second paragraph with: “I also worked with Git/GitHub as part of the development workflow.”

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the third paragraph, replace the repetitive sentence beginning “My experience with automated unit testing...” with a more concise, role-focused sentence: “This experience with automated unit testing, Storybook, and Git-based workflows would provide a practical foundation for contributing to a collaborative Patient Experience squad.” This uses the job ad’s terminology without claiming end-to-end testing.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the closing paragraph, make the contribution more specific by changing “how my experience and approach could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team” to “how my experience building accessible React interfaces and full-stack academic projects could contribute to Verdane Care’s patient-facing features.”

I also worked with Git/GitHub as part of the development workflow. In my Tidewatch project, I developed a React and TypeScript interface and a Node.js/Express API backed by PostgreSQL. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver, and it achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.

I would bring a practical, user-focused approach to building patient-facing features, with a strong interest in accessibility. My freelance work also includes building a Next.js booking website for a yoga studio, giving me experience with a wellness-related booking context, Next.js, and static generation. This experience with automated unit testing, Storybook, and Git-based workflows would provide a practical foundation for contributing to a collaborative Patient Experience squad.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building accessible React interfaces and full-stack academic projects could contribute to Verdane Care’s patient-facing features.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team. It presents credible evidence from the internship, Tidewatch project, and freelance work rather than relying on generic claims. The strongest points are the quantified accessibility work across 20+ components, the Lighthouse score of 100, and the clear connection between the candidate’s experience and patient-facing software. The main content issue is a slight overstatement in the closing reference to “full-stack academic projects,” since the source material clearly identifies one full-stack project, Tidewatch, while Study Buddy was primarily frontend work.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses several relevant job-description terms naturally, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Next.js, and patient-facing features. Its plain structure and standard paragraphs are easy to parse. It does not claim unsupported Playwright, NestJS, Docker, AWS, OWASP, or healthcare experience, which is appropriate. Since the employer says the cover letter is optional, ATS impact will be secondary to the CV; the letter supports screening for the candidate’s demonstrated technologies but cannot overcome the documented gaps in 2+ years of professional experience, end-to-end testing, and security fundamentals.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the supported parts of the role: accessible React interfaces, TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, unit testing, Git-based work, Storybook, Next.js, and wellness-related booking software. The motivation is appropriately connected to Verdane Care’s patients-first and human-centred mission. The letter does not demonstrate the must-have requirement of 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript experience; the source material shows an internship and freelance experience but not two years. It also does not establish end-to-end testing, web security or OWASP awareness, privacy requirements for health data, semantic HTML and responsive layouts specifically, German or Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A/B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps or unsupported requirements, not defects that should be addressed by making unsupported claims. The teaching-assistant experience could also support the role’s mentoring aspect but is currently omitted.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the final paragraph, replace “full-stack academic projects” with “my full-stack Tidewatch project” or “my academic full-stack project, Tidewatch.” This keeps the claim precise because the source material identifies Tidewatch as full-stack, while Study Buddy involved building the React frontend and login screens rather than the backend and database.

MINOR — In the third paragraph, after the sentence about the freelance yoga-studio website, add a concise mentoring example such as: “As a teaching assistant for a first-year web development lab, I also supported approximately 30 students during one semester.” This is fully supported by the candidate information and gives direct evidence relevant to Verdane Care’s interest in mentoring junior colleagues, without adding unsupported claims.

MINOR — In the second paragraph, consider changing “I also worked with Git/GitHub as part of the development workflow” to “I also have experience with Git/GitHub and Git-based development workflows.” This wording aligns more closely with the documented Skills section and avoids implying a specific level of professional workflow ownership that is not detailed in the source material.
critique.critical_issues:
The phrase “full-stack academic projects” is potentially misleading because the candidate information clearly supports one full-stack academic project, Tidewatch; Study Buddy was a frontend contribution with other team members responsible for the API and database. Revise this wording as specified in the improvement instructions.

- "substantial academic projects building accessible web applications"
- "full-stack academic projects"
